title: 0992 Time to Therapy Initiation for Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Children

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title> <jats:p>Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is associated with neuro-cognitive, cardiovascular, and metabolic morbidity in children, with those with severe OSA being at a higher risk. Timely initiation of appropriate therapy is key to reducing morbidity from severe OSA. This Quality Improvement project’s goal was to perform a baseline evaluation of the time to initial therapy initiation in children with severe OSA at our institution as a first step to address barriers to timely intervention.</jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Methods</jats:title> <jats:p>A chart review was completed for all patients diagnosed with severe OSA at Nationwide Children’s Hospital sleep laboratory from January-September 2023. Severe OSA was defined as an AHI of ≥ 10 or greater, and urgent intervention was defined as therapy initiation within 48 hours.</jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Results</jats:title> <jats:p>216 patients met inclusion criteria with 51 children age < 1 yr., 13 children age ≥1 to < 2 yrs., and 152 children age ≥2yrs. Urgent intervention was taken in 75% (n=38) of children age < 1 yr., 38% (n=5) of children age ≥1 to < 2 yrs., and 13% (n=20) of children age ≥2 yrs. Intervention was completed within 14 days in 84% (n=43) of children age < 1 yr., 46% (n=6) of children age ≥1 to < 2 yrs., and 24% (n=37) of children age ≥2 yrs. Oxygen supplementation was the initial intervention in 86.5% (n=44) of children age < 1 yr., 38.4% (n=5) of children age ≥1 to < 2 yrs., and 6.5% (n=10) of children age ≥2 yrs. Positive airway pressure therapy was the initial intervention in 0.2% (n=1) of children age < 1 yr., 23% (n=3) of children age ≥1to< 2 yrs., and 51.3% (n=78) of children age ≥2 yrs. Surgical intervention in patients without prior adenotonsillectomy was completed in 21.5% (n=11) of children age < 1yr., 53.8% (n=7) of children age ≥1 to < 2 yrs., and 67.5% (n=73) of children age ≥2 yrs.</jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title> <jats:p>A multidisciplinary collaborative approach is important in timely initiation of management in children with severe OSA. The time to intervention and type of intervention selected differed across age groups. Barriers to timely intervention will be addressed in future projects using quality improvement methodology.</jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Support (if any)</jats:title> <jats:p> </jats:p> </jats:sec>
